description: Core Stage A host-element color-ID feasibility campaign: can Stage A reliably assign unique colors to visible host Revit elements and export a raster from which those elements can be recovered, across elevation/plan(active)/plan(inactive)/RCP/section/callout. External-source and additional-semantic-diagnostic work is intentionally out of scope here - see examples/stage_a_followup_campaign.json.

stages.description: Elevation reference view: confirm a viable minimum-mutation recipe (attached_AS, falling back to detached_AS only if template-blocked) and, in the same job, produce the reviewable elevation host color-ID raster - the recipe-confirmation raster IS the elevation Stage 3 validation artifact, so it is never re-rendered a second time just to be reviewed.

jobs.manual_review_reason: Does this raster accurately represent the visible host-model elements and their boundaries/occlusion for this view, with annotations/non-model graphics excluded as intended and without obvious color contamination that would prevent element-ID recovery?

stages.description: Confirm the chosen export resolution/alignment policy (150 DPI, mode=all) is technically usable: twice at the elevation reference view (determinism), once per remaining core view (each view's bounds/geometry resolution is a distinct technical case). No repeated multi-DPI/fixed-width experimentation here - that belongs to the non-blocking resolution-sensitivity follow-up campaign.

Apply the single recipe selected at Stage 1 (attached_AS, with the same per-view template-block fallback safety net) to each remaining core view at the single confirmed resolution policy, producing one reviewable host color-ID raster per view. No full mutation-variant factorial is run here.

host_color_id_feasibility.description: Aggregate host-element color-ID feasibility conclusion, derived from the terminal status of each core view's mutation-recipe closure (see conditional_fallbacks). A view is PASS only once its closure resolved on a candidate job that reached PASSED - which itself requires every automated technical gate (attestation, rollback, state restoration, TIFF dimensions, palette fidelity) plus an ACCEPTED operator visual review, never an automated pass alone. See campaign_planner.host_color_id_feasibility().
